data.text:
Decentral × Tanssi: Bringing Real World Finance Onchain for LATAM’s Creative Economy

LATAM’s creative economy is massive; advertising agencies, production studios, independent creators, but most of them face the same bottleneck:
slow payments, expensive credit, and opaque financing. 

This is why @usedecentral wants to fix this by bringing receivable financing onchain.

1. Why the creative economy needs onchain finance:

In LATAM, creators and agencies rarely own dependable financing. Payments take weeks, sometimes months.
Debt is expensive, and lower-tier creators have almost no access to formal credit.

Decentral’s model provides onchain liquidity pools that fund future receivables, giving creators predictable cashflow.

2. Real-Time indicators that shows LATAM creator-economy realities:

•$45B+ LATAM creator economy value (Influencity 2024).
•35–60 days average invoice settlement for agencies + creators in Brazil & Argentina.
•Up to 30% annualized cost of capital for small creative businesses seeking upfront liquidity.
•35%+ year on year growth in alternative finance demand across LATAM SMEs.

These conditions make Decentral’s model onchain liquidity for off chain cash flows extremely relevant.

⸻

3. Why @TanssiNetwork is the right foundation:

Decentral needs predictable execution, low fees, and sovereign control.
Tanssi gives them:
•a dedicated appchain
•permissionless operator security
•cross chain liquidity routing
•automated block production + sequencing
•zero infra overhead

In short: Decentral gets L1 power without L1 complexity.

⸻

4. Case Studies LATAM creators who would benefit:

🟣 Brazilian ad agencies
Often wait 60+ days for brand payments.
A Decentral pool could unlock early liquidity, more campaigns, customer growth.

🟠 Argentinian production studios
Inflation makes delayed payments harmful.
Tokenized receivables on a Tanssi powered chain mean they can access capital instantly at transparent rates.

🔵 Independent musicians & creators
Streaming platforms pay in 30–45 day cycles.
Onchain factoring lets them pull forward future revenue in hours, not weeks.

These are real, persistent problems and Decentral’s structure aligns perfectly with them.

⸻

5. Comparisons: Why Tanssi? 

Because existing stacks don’t match the needs of RWF protocols:
• OP Stack = shared sequencers → congestion risk
• Solana = high performance but no control over fees or blockspace
• Cosmos SDK = slow validator bootstrapping & high overhead
• Avalanche Subnets = security depends entirely on your own validator set

Tanssi gives Decentral the best of both worlds:
Sovereignty + shared security + guaranteed throughput + automated infra.
A chain they own, without the cost of building one.

6. Why this model could scale beyond LATAM:

If Decentral succeeds:
•African creator markets (Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa) have the same payment-latency problems.
•Southeast Asia’s independent work economy (Philippines, Indonesia) is booming with similar credit gaps.

The rails they’re building on Tanssi can travel globally.

⸻

7. Personal Insight

Real-world finance protocols rarely succeed because the infrastructure cost is too high and the settlement flow is too unpredictable.
Decentral avoids both problems by launching on Tanssi:
•Their receivables become tokenized, composable instruments.
•Their financing pools operate on a sovereign chain with guaranteed throughput.
•Their settlement is fully verifiable onchain, making underwriting far cleaner.

If this model works in LATAM; one of the world’s most fragmented creative economies, it becomes a blueprint for emerging markets everywhere.

Student Lars spent 1.5 years with some other YouTube Automation course

Got nowhere & made like $200 total... learned all the wrong strategies

Then he joined my program and everything changed

- Monetized in 6 weeks
- $5K/month by week 10
- $10K+ months consistently
- Almost $100K in under a year

Now he quit his job and is heading to Bali for a few months lol

So what actually changed for Lars? 👇🏼

1) He STOPPED trying to reinvent the wheel

Lars was trying to be creative/unique with his videos. I told him to just find what's working and clone it (but better). He started doing that and boom... views came flooding in ;)

2) He focused on ONE channel instead of spreading himself thin

Most people want to start 5 channels at once. Lars went all in on one niche, one format, one strategy until it worked

3) He treated this like a real business

Hired a solid team from the Philippines. $400-500/month per person. Built systems so he could step back. That's when things really scaled

4) He came PREPARED to every call

Asked specific questions & took notes. Actually implemented what we talked about. Most people just show up and expect magic without doing the work

Lars literally told me: I had to forget everything I learned before and think like you

I teach you to keep it stupidly simple and focus on what actually makes money

Lars went through channel terminations and all the bullshit. But he didn't quit

Now he's coaching students himself and getting them results too

His goal for 2026... $50K+ months

And honestly I think he'll hit it

data.text:
All 17 Metro Manila local government units received today one Patient Transport Vehicles (PTVs) each from the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) aimed at strengthening the local emergency medical response capacities in the National Capital Region.

PCSO General Manager Mel Robles, in a ceremony held during the Metro Manila Council (MMC) meeting, handed over the keys of the PTVs to several local chief executives present.

The initiative is in fulfilment of the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. to equip all cities, provinces, and municipalities with PTVs under the Medical Transport Vehicular Donation Program (MTVDP), a key government strategy to strengthen universal access to emergency medical care.

"Metro Manila is the heart of our nation, home to millions of Filipinos. And while we have major hospitals and healthcare facilities here, we also know that traffic, distance, and accessibility remain real challenges. These Patient Transport Vehicles will help bridge that gap, ensuring that when emergencies happen, help can arrive quickly," said Robles, adding that  "100% of PTVs have been distributed, all LGUs nationwide are now equipped with these lifesaving vehicles."

Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) Chairman Atty. Don Artes, who presided over the meeting, expressed gratitude to the President and the PCSO for the support extended to the Metro Manila LGUs, citing that the distributed PTVs are a significant boost to the LGUs' local health care system. 

"The life-saving PTV plays a crucial role in addressing medical emergencies, disaster response, and transportation needs within their respective localities, which is part of the administration's broader goal of building Bagong Pilipinas, where quality healthcare is accessible, efficient, and closer to the Filipinos," said Artes.
